\label{lemma-regular-local-ring-local}
Let $f : U \to V$ be an \'etale morphism of schemes.
Let $u \in U$ and $v = f(u)$. Then
$\mathcal{O}_{U, u}$ is a regular local ring if and only if
$\mathcal{O}_{V, v}$ is a regular local ring.
statement: Let $f:U\to V$ be an étale morphism of schemes, $u\in U$, $v=f(u)$. The local ring $\mathcal O_{U,u}$ is regular if and only if $\mathcal O_{V,v}$ is regular (a regular local ring is Noetherian and its maximal ideal has a minimal generating set of cardinality equal to its Krull dimension).
conclusions: Regularity of the local rings is equivalent.
equivalence_sides: O_(U,u) is a regular local ring iff O_(V,v) is a regular local ring.

\label{lemma-pullback-property-local-target}
Let $\tau \in \{fpqc, fppf, syntomic, smooth, \etale, Zariski\}$.
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a property of morphisms which is $\tau$ local
on the target. Let $f : X \to Y$ have property $\mathcal{P}$.
For any morphism $Y' \to Y$ which is
flat, resp.\ flat and locally of finite presentation, resp.\ syntomic,
resp.\ \'etale, resp.\ an open immersion, the base change
$f' : Y' \times_Y X \to Y'$ of $f$ has property $\mathcal{P}$.
statement: A property $\mathcal P$ of scheme morphisms is *local on the target for the $\tau$-topology* if for every $\tau$-covering $\{Y_i\to Y\}$, a morphism $f:X\to Y$ has $\mathcal P$ if and only if each base-changed morphism $f_i:X\times_YY_i\to Y_i$ has $\mathcal P$. Let $\tau$ be one of fpqc, fppf, syntomic, smooth, étale, or Zariski, and let $\mathcal P$ be $\tau$-local on the target. If $f:X\to Y$ has $\mathcal P$, then its base change along any $g:Y'\to Y$ belonging to the corresponding class of maps—flat for fpqc; flat locally finitely presented for fppf; syntomic for syntomic; smooth for smooth; étale for étale; and an open immersion for Zariski—also has $\mathcal P$.
hypotheses: P is tau-local on the target; f has P; g belongs to the indicated class for tau.
conclusions: The base change f':X×_Y Y'→Y' has P.

\label{lemma-largest-open-of-the-base}
Let $\tau \in \{fppf, syntomic, smooth, \etale\}$.
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a property of morphisms which is $\tau$ local
on the target. For any morphism of schemes $f : X \to Y$ there exists
a largest open $W(f) \subset Y$ such that the restriction
$X_{W(f)} \to W(f)$ has $\mathcal{P}$. Moreover,
\begin{enumerate}
\item if $g : Y' \to Y$ is flat and locally of finite presentation,
syntomic, smooth, or \'etale and the base change $f' : X_{Y'} \to Y'$
has $\mathcal{P}$, then $g(Y') \subset W(f)$,
\item if $g : Y' \to Y$ is flat and locally of finite presentation,
syntomic, smooth, or \'etale, then $W(f') = g^{-1}(W(f))$, and
\item if $\{g_i : Y_i \to Y\}$ is a $\tau$-covering, then
$g_i^{-1}(W(f)) = W(f_i)$, where $f_i$ is the base change of $f$
by $Y_i \to Y$.
\end{enumerate}

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-descending-properties-morphisms}
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a property of morphisms of schemes over a base.
Let $\tau \in \{fpqc, fppf, \etale, smooth, syntomic\}$.
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item the property is preserved under
flat, flat and locally of finite presentation, \'etale, smooth, or syntomic
base change depending on whether $\tau$ is fpqc, fppf, \'etale, smooth, or
syntomic (compare with
Schemes, Definition \ref{schemes-definition-preserved-by-base-change}),
\item the property is Zariski local on the base.
\item for any surjective morphism of affine schemes $S' \to S$
which is flat, flat of finite presentation,
\'etale, smooth or syntomic depending on whether $\tau$ is
fpqc, fppf, \'etale, smooth, or syntomic,
and any morphism of schemes $f : X \to S$ property
$\mathcal{P}$ holds for $f$ if property $\mathcal{P}$
holds for the base change $f' : X' = S' \times_S X \to S'$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $\mathcal{P}$ is $\tau$ local on the base.
statement: A property $\mathcal P$ of scheme morphisms is *local on the target for the $\tau$-topology* if for every $\tau$-covering $\{Y_i\to Y\}$, a morphism $f:X\to Y$ has $\mathcal P$ if and only if each base-changed morphism $f_i:X\times_YY_i\to Y_i$ has $\mathcal P$. Let $\tau$ be one of fpqc, fppf, étale, smooth, or syntomic, and suppose $\mathcal P$ satisfies all three assumptions: (1) $\mathcal P$ is preserved under base change by, respectively, flat morphisms (fpqc), flat locally finitely presented morphisms (fppf), étale morphisms (étale), smooth morphisms (smooth), or syntomic morphisms (syntomic); (2) $\mathcal P$ is local on the target for Zariski open coverings; (3) for any surjective morphism $S'\to S$ of affine schemes of the corresponding type and any scheme morphism $f:X\to S$, $\mathcal P$ for $f\times_SS'$ implies $\mathcal P$ for $f$. Then $\mathcal P$ is local on the target for arbitrary $\tau$-coverings.
hypotheses: P stable under the relevant base changes, Zariski-local on target and descending through surjective affine maps of the chosen type.
conclusions: P is tau-local on the target.

\label{lemma-universally-injective-etale-open-immersion}
A universally injective \'etale morphism is an open immersion.
statement: For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of schemes, *universally injective* means that the underlying map of topological spaces remains injective after every base change (equivalently, $f$ is radicial). This is distinct from the pure-ring-map condition used earlier in the module-descent chapter. If $f:X\to Y$ is an étale morphism of schemes and is universally injective in this scheme-morphism sense, then $f$ is an open immersion.
hypotheses: f is étale and universally injective/radicial as a scheme morphism.
conclusions: f identifies X with an open subscheme of Y.

\label{lemma-descending-property-proper-over-base}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes which is locally of finite type.
Let $Z$ be a closed subset of $X$. If there exists an fpqc covering
$\{Y_i \to Y\}$ such that the inverse image $Z_i \subset Y_i \times_Y X$
is proper over $Y_i$
(Cohomology of Schemes, Definition \ref{coherent-definition-proper-over-base})
then $Z$ is proper over $Y$.
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a locally finite type morphism of schemes and $Z\subseteq|X|$ a closed subset. Endow $Z$ with the reduced induced closed subscheme structure $Z_{\mathrm{red}}\hookrightarrow X$. Say that the closed subset $Z$ is *proper over $Y$* if $Z_{\mathrm{red}}\to Y$ is proper. Suppose there is an fpqc covering $\{Y_i\to Y\}$ such that the inverse-image closed subset $Z_i\subseteq|X\times_YY_i|$ is proper over $Y_i$ (with the same reduced-induced-subscheme convention). Then $Z$ is proper over $Y$.
hypotheses: f locally finite type, Z closed, and inverse-image closed subsets are proper after an fpqc covering of Y.

\label{lemma-descending-property-ample}
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $\{g_i : S_i \to S\}_{i \in I}$ be an fpqc covering.
Let $f_i : X_i \to S_i$ be the base change of $f$ and let $\mathcal{L}_i$
be the pullback of $\mathcal{L}$ to $X_i$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{L}$ is ample on $X/S$, and
\item $\mathcal{L}_i$ is ample on $X_i/S_i$
for every $i \in I$.
\end{enumerate}
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a scheme morphism, $\mathcal L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module, and $\{g_i:S_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ an fpqc covering. Put $X_i=X\times_SS_i$, let $f_i:X_i\to S_i$ be the structure morphisms, and $\mathcal L_i$ the respective pullbacks of $\mathcal L$. Then $\mathcal L$ is relatively ample for $f$ (ample on $X/S$) if and only if every $\mathcal L_i$ is relatively ample for $f_i$.
hypotheses: L is invertible on X, with an fpqc base covering of S.
conclusions: Relative ampleness can be checked after the fpqc covering.
equivalence_sides: L is ample relative to X/S iff every L_i is ample relative to X_i/S_i.
